grades.quote: FMV.X.D and FMV.D.X do not modify the bits being transferred; in particular, the payloads of noncanonical NaNs are preserved.
grades.reason: Covers the double-precision analogues FMV.X.D/FMV.D.X, not FMV.X.W. It states that these moves transfer bit patterns without modifying them, which is the representation-transfer principle behind the query. It does not mention FCVT.W.S or the single-precision instructions.

This is an encoding table for the half-precision Zfh instructions (FMV.X.H, FCVT.W.H). It says nothing about FMV.X.W or FCVT.W.S, and it does not explain the difference between a move and a conversion.

grades.quote: FCVT.W.S or FCVT.L.S converts a floating-point number in floating-point register _rs1_ to a signed 32-bit or 64-bit integer, respectively, in integer register _rd_ .
grades.reason: Describes FCVT.W.S as a numeric conversion of a float to a signed 32-bit integer. It says the conversion rounds according to rm, clips out-of-range values, and sets the invalid and inexact flags. This covers the conversion side of the contrast. The visible text does not describe FMV.X.W, so the bit-transfer side is missing.
This is a register-dependency table for the RV64-only instructions FCVT.L.S, FCVT.LU.S, FCVT.S.L and FCVT.S.LU. It does not cover FCVT.W.S or FMV.X.W, and it gives no explanation of how they differ.
